phase: ROADMAP Stage 2B: claim-to-evidence lexical mapping v1
implemented: Added map_claim_to_evidence(claim, evidence_items) as a deterministic lexical attribution helper over search_library items.
Exposed verify_claim.evidence_map with required_markers, covered_markers, missing_markers, supporting_items, and coverage_ratio.
covered_markers is now {marker: [chunk_id, ...]}, ordered by retrieval rank and deduped, so a marker covered in multiple chunks is preserved.
verify_claim keeps the conservative status rule: any missing required marker prevents supported status.
cited_chunk_ids now prefers chunks that actually matched required markers, then backfills from top retrieved chunks.
Added ClaimEvidenceMapTest coverage for fully covered markers, missing markers, multi-chunk marker attribution, pure text claims, empty evidence, and HTTP JSON round-trip.
Updated README and retrieval/architecture/roadmap docs to state that this is lexical coverage, not semantic entailment or conflict detection.
not_implemented: Semantic entailment and conflict evidence detection are still out of scope for this stage and require later LLM/NLI work.
A real anonymized 50-100 case retrieval/claim verification evaluation set is still not built.
Vector retrieval, embeddings, vector storage, and semantic reranking are still not implemented.
UI-level evidence highlighting and visual citation-chain review are still not implemented.
test_commands: python -m py_compile backend/server.py tests/test_library.py tools/evaluate_retrieval.py tools/run_quality_gates.py tests/test_quality_gates.py
test_status: Codex verified on Windows review repo: py_compile passed; unittest discover ran 88 tests OK; tools/run_quality_gates.py --json returned passed=true with 5 gates passed; git diff --check passed; independent rg credential scan found no secret-shaped tokens.
dependencies: Implementation uses Python standard library only.
No network, npm, embedding service, or LLM call is required for this feature.
review_notes: Claude's first implementation used a single chunk_id per marker; Codex rejected it because the stage required all covering chunks. The返工 version now uses marker -> [chunk_id, ...] and passes the added multi-chunk test.
The evidence mapping is deterministic and reproducible, but it is lexical attribution only. It must not be represented as proof of semantic entailment.
Downstream consumers must treat covered_markers values as lists, not scalars.
risks: Lexical overlap can still be false-positive when the same number or year appears in unrelated context.
The order of chunks for a marker follows retrieval rank; it is not a separate authority-first order.
Any downstream script or UI that already assumed covered_markers[marker] was a scalar must be updated.
